TIL that all tequila is actually mezcal. Mezcal is a distilled spirit made from any type of agave plant. Tequila can only be made from blue agave in Jalisco. Under the NOM-070 Mezcal standard, the Jalisco state is excluded from geographic origin so no tequila can be legally called mezcal.

TIL about Kaihōgyō, a practice performed by Japanese Buddhist monks. It takes 7 years to complete and involves walking up to 84 km a day every day for months and a period of not eating, drinking or sleeping for 9 days. Historically, those who couldn't complete it had to kill themselves.
TIL I learned that Antarctica has a full-time professional fire department and as of 2025 maintains 55 staff.

TIL that during the premiere of Ode to Joy, an almost deaf Ludwig van Beethoven had to be turned around by a singer to receive the audience’s applause as he was several bars behind and still conducting the orchestra
TIL that Chinese men in Hong Kong could legally take concubines according to the legal code of the Qing Dynasty until 1971.
TIL in the aftermath of the failed Bay of Pigs invasion, the US and Cuba agreed to settle for $53 million(about $591 million today) of baby food and medicine in exchange for prisoners.

TIL about Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder, or ARFID, an eating disorder which causes sufferers to majorly limit the amount of food they eat. Unlike other eating disorders, it isn't caused by body image issues, but by issues with the sensory details of foods, such as their texture or taste.

TIL of the Big Four, which are four species of highly venomous snakes (Russell's viper, common krait, Indian cobra, and Indian saw-scaled viper) responsible for causing the most snake bite medical cases in India. Each year, around 46,000 to 60,000 people die from their bites.

TIL that in the 1850s a French merchant named Joseph Limantour presented forged documents that granted him 20,000 acres encompassing almost all of San Fransisco. After three years of deliberation, his claim was approved by the government. His fraud as later exposed in court, and he fled to Mexico.
TIL that until 2022 US surveyors still used the "survey foot", dating from the 1890s. The "survey inch" was about 25.4000508 mm instead of the EXACT 25.4 mm everyone else used.
